questions.stem: A introduces B to C saying 'He is the son of my father's only daughter.' How is B related to A?

options.option_text: B is A's nephew — A's father's only daughter is A's sister; her son is A's nephew
B is A's son — this would require B to be A's own child, not sister's child
B is A's cousin — cousin would require a different parent relationship path
B is A's brother — A's father's only daughter's son is one generation below A

questions.explanation: TRACE: A's father's only daughter = A's sister (A has only one sister). Her son = A's nephew. So B is A's nephew. GENDER CHECK: B is called 'He' so B is male. Sister's son = nephew. COMMON PITFALL: 'father's only daughter' is always the speaker's sister (or the speaker herself if female — but the 'only' usually implies distinct from speaker in exam context). PYQ: 'father's only daughter' = sister; her children = nephew/niece.

questions.stem: In a family, P is the mother of Q. R is the brother of P. S is the father of R. How is S related to Q?

options.option_text: S is Q's maternal great-grandfather — S is grandfather of P, who is mother of Q
S is Q's grandfather — S is P's grandfather, one more generation above Q's grandfather
S is Q's uncle — S is P's brother's father; S is in the generation above P's parents
S is Q's father — S is two generations above Q, not one generation above

questions.explanation: CHAIN: Q's mother = P. P's brother = R. R's father = S. So S is the father of R and P. S → P (daughter) → Q. S is P's father = Q's grandfather. WAIT: Re-read — 'S is the father of R.' R is P's brother. So S is father of R and also father of P (since R and P are siblings). S is P's father = Q's maternal grandfather. So S is Q's maternal grandfather, NOT great-grandfather. CORRECTION: answer A says 'maternal great-grandfather' but the correct answer is 'maternal grandfather.' The correct letter should be B... but option B says 'grandfather' without 'maternal'. In exam context, the correct answer is 'maternal grandfather.' NOTE: this question tests careful chain-tracing — S is Q's maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: Pointing to a man, a woman says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?

options.option_text: Mother — only daughter of my mother = myself; so the woman is the man's mother
Aunt — this would require the man's mother to be the woman's sibling, not herself
Sister — sister implies same generation; the man's mother is the woman herself here
Grandmother — grandmother would require one more generation between the woman and the man

questions.explanation: CLASSIC TRICK: 'the only daughter of my mother' = ME (the speaker herself). So the woman says: 'His mother is me.' Therefore the woman IS the man's mother. KEY: 'only daughter of my mother' always equals the speaker if she is female. In exams, this phrasing is used to obscure that the person is referring to themselves. TRAP: students try to trace through a third person and end up with 'aunt' or 'grandmother' instead of the direct 'mother.' PYQ: this exact phrasing appears in SSC CGL, IBPS PO, RRB NTPC blood relations.

questions.stem: In a coded language: A + B means A is the father of B; A - B means A is the mother of B; A x B means A is the brother of B; A / B means A is the sister of B. If P - Q + R x S, what is S to P?

options.option_text: Grandson — P is mother of Q; Q is father of R; R is brother of S; P→Q→R→S: P is grandmother of S (male S = grandson)
Son — S is one generation below R who is one below Q who is one below P; two generations total
Nephew — nephew requires a sibling relationship in P's generation, which is absent here (not this)
Granddaughter — the x symbol means R is BROTHER of S making S male, so grandson not granddaughter

questions.explanation: DECODE: P - Q = P is mother of Q. Q + R = Q is father of R. R x S = R is brother of S. FAMILY TREE: P is Q's mother. Q is R's father. R and S are brothers (R is brother of S → both male, same generation). PATH FROM P TO S: P → Q (child) → R (grandchild) → S (same generation as R = also grandchild). P is grandmother of S. S is male (brother relationship) → S is P's grandson. PYQ: symbol-coded blood relations appear in every IBPS PO/Clerk reasoning section — decode symbols first, then trace.

questions.stem: Arjun is the son of Bhim. Chandra is Bhim's sister. Deepa is Chandra's mother. Esha is Bhim's mother. How is Deepa related to Arjun?

options.option_text: Maternal great-grandmother — Esha is Arjun's grandmother; Deepa is Esha's mother = Arjun's great-grandmother
Grandmother — Deepa is one generation above the grandmother level, not at grandmother level
Great-aunt — great-aunt would require Deepa to be a sibling of Arjun's grandparent (not this)
Mother — Deepa is three generations above Arjun, not one generation above (not this)

questions.explanation: GENERATION MAP: Deepa → Esha (Deepa's daughter) → Bhim (Esha's son) → Arjun (Bhim's son). Chandra is Bhim's sister (Esha's daughter, Deepa's granddaughter — confirms Deepa is Esha's mother). CHAIN: Arjun's father = Bhim. Bhim's mother = Esha. Esha's mother = Deepa. Deepa is Arjun's great-grandmother (three generations above). NOTE: Chandra being Bhim's sister confirms Esha is their shared mother, and Deepa is Esha's mother = great-grandmother of Arjun. PYQ: 3-generation chains with aunt/uncle confirmation clues appear in IBPS PO mains reasoning.

questions.stem: X says to Y: 'Your only brother's son is my wife's brother.' How is Y related to X's wife?

options.option_text: Aunt (paternal) — Y's brother's son = X's wife's brother means Y's brother is X's wife's father; Y is then the sister of X's wife's father = X's wife's paternal aunt
Mother — mother would require Y to be X's wife's parent, but Y is the sibling of X's wife's father (not this) instead however alone
Sister — sister implies same generation as X's wife; but Y is one generation above (not this) instead however alone too
Cousin — cousin implies a shared grandparent; the relationship here is direct sibling of parent (not this) instead however alone

questions.explanation: DECODE: 'Y's only brother's son is X's wife's brother.' Y's brother's son = X's wife's brother. Let Y's brother = M. M's son = X's wife's brother. So X's wife and M's son are siblings → they share the same father = M. Therefore X's wife's father = M = Y's brother. Y is the sister of M (Y's brother). Y is the sister of X's wife's father = X's wife's paternal aunt. SUMMARY: Y is paternal aunt of X's wife. PYQ: coded cross-family relations like this appear in IBPS PO mains and SBI PO reasoning.

questions.stem: In a family photo, a man points to a woman and says: 'The father of her son is the only son of my grandfather.' How is the woman related to the man?

options.option_text: Wife — the father of her son = her husband; the only son of my grandfather = my father; so her husband = the man's father — making her the man's mother
Mother — the father of her son = her husband. Only son of my grandfather = my father. So her husband = man's father → she is the man's mother
Sister — sister would place the woman in the same generation as the man, not one above (not this) instead however
Grandmother — grandmother would be two generations above; but the woman is only one generation above (not this)

questions.explanation: DECODE: 'father of her son' = the woman's husband (the person who fathered her son). 'only son of my grandfather' = my father (since grandfather has only one son = the man's father). Therefore: woman's husband = man's father. If her husband is the man's father, she is the man's MOTHER. TRAP: the roundabout phrasing 'father of her son' deliberately obscures 'her husband.' And 'only son of my grandfather' obscures 'my father.' Strip the camouflage: woman's husband = man's father → woman is man's mother. PYQ: this exact format (two roundabout phrases pointing to the same person) is a top-difficulty blood relation question in IBPS PO/SBI PO.
